title: Competition and Consumer Amendment (Australian Country of Origin Food Labelling) Bill 2013

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would create country of origin labelling rules for packaged and unpackaged food sold at retail, with specified Australian origin and processing claims.
Manufactured in Australia claims would require substantial transformation and at least 50 per cent of transformation costs incurred locally, replacing Made in Australia claims.
The rules would begin after a 12-month transition following Royal Assent, with penalty exemptions for food supplied for immediate consumption by specified institutions.
changes: Product of Australia claims would require all significant ingredients and all processing to be Australian.
Packaged food with minimal Australian processing but no substantial transformation in Australia would use the Packaged in Australia label.
Country of origin labelling breaches would attract new civil and criminal penalties.
Courts could disqualify people from managing corporations for involvement in labelling contraventions.
summary.affected: Food businesses supplying packaged or unpackaged retail food and consumers reading country of origin labels are affected.
